analyst_view.overall: Sunderland (11th, 7 pts) host Jagiellonia (29th, 3 pts) needing a win to stay near the top eight, after a 2-0 home defeat to Dinamo Zagreb last time in Europe. They drew 0-0 at Aston Villa on Saturday but are in the Premier League bottom three and host Tottenham on Sunday, so changes are likely, with Danso, Alderete and Methalie pushing for starts. Granit Xhaka (calf, no return date), Brian Brobbey (thigh), Ballard, Mundle and Diarra are out; the numbers count Brobbey (about -23% on Sunderland's goals) and Diarra but not Xhaka or rotation. Correcting my earlier view: Sports Mole's preview says Trai Hume is one booking from a ban, not banned, and has Taras Romanczuk in Jagiellonia's expected XI (his suspension looks like a league one); Jagiellonia lost 3-1 at Cracovia, have Ousmane Sow doubtful and no away fans. Bulgarian referee Georgi Kabakov (about 4.6 cards a game) is in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already take a big slice off Sunderland for Brobbey, with their poor recent scoring (3 in six) also counted. Xhaka's absence and likely rotation before Spurs are not in the numbers, so I trim a little, to about 2.1; Sunderland have scored more than once in only one of their last nine home games.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 7.3 for Sunderland, already a little lower for their recent corner count. Without Xhaka to set the tempo and with changes likely, Sunderland's pressure should be a bit lighter, though Hume is available after all, so I go only to about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, already raised for both sides' recent bookings and for referee Georgi Kabakov's above-average record (4.6 a game). Hume, one yellow from a ban, may be careful or rested, but that is too small to move, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots, mostly Sunderland (21.4), already up about 8% for their recent shooting. Rotation with Spurs three days later and no Xhaka should trim that a little, so I go to about 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, and Sunderland have scored with under 5% of their shots in this phase. A rotated attack around Wilson Isidor should be slightly less sharp, so I go to about 9.5.
